Contexts chosen arbitrarily by Nature (arbitrary sequence)
settings.definition_quote: In each round t = 1, . . . , T : 1. Nature chooses an arbitrary joint context assignment x^t_C, which is observed by the learning algorithm. 2. The learning algorithm chooses a joint action assignment x^t_A. 3. The learning algorithm receives an independent random payoff f^t \in [0, 1] with expectation F(x^t_A, x^t_C). ... Assumption 1 (Payoff Decomposition). We are given a collection of variable subsets P such that F(x) = \sum_{P} f_P(x_P)

algorithms.name: GraphicalBandits (BestAct + PayEst KWIK linear regression)
requires_knowledge_of: payoff decomposition structure P / tree decomposition of action subgraph

symbols.d: rank of the coefficient matrix M (dimension of the span of coefficient vectors)
symbols.w: treewidth of the tree decomposition of the action subgraph
symbols.m_dom: maximum domain size max_i |X_i| of a variable
symbols.n_E: number of edges |E| of the tree decomposition
symbols.delta: failure probability parameter given to PayEst

conditions: Expected payoff decomposes as in Assumption 1 with known P
tuning: PayEst = KWIK linear regression of Cesa-Bianchi et al. (2009) with parameters epsilon, delta

source.quote: Let d = rank(M) be the rank of the coefficient matrix, and let T = (A, E) be the tree decomposition of the action subgraph GA with treewidth w. The regret R(T) of GraphicalBandits after T rounds is at most R(T) \le O(dw/\epsilon^2 log(T m|E|/\epsilon\delta) + 2|A|\epsilon T + \delta T) and the computational complexity of each round is O(m^{2w}|E|).

results.notes: Per-round computation O(m^{2w}|E|): polynomial for constant treewidth (exponential in w). The algorithm does not need T for fixed eps, delta, hence marked anytime. Section 7.1 gives an informal refinement for i.i.d. contexts from distribution D: R(T) <= T P(x_C in X'_C) + O(rank(M(not X'_C)) w |A| T^{2/3} log(T m|E|)) (not recorded separately).
